1. The Offer

  • Subjects & Topics: What specific subjects, skills, or exams do you teach (e.g., math, language, test prep)?

  • Format & Delivery: Will you teach online, in-person, one-to-one, or in groups?

2. The Ideal Student

  • Target Audience: Who are you teaching (e.g., primary school students, adults, corporate clients)?

  • Core Need: What specific problem or goal brings them to you (e.g., passing a state exam, learning conversational fluency)?

3. Pricing & Packages

  • Rates: What is your hourly or per-session rate?

  • Bundles: Do you sell discounted multi-lesson packs or monthly subscriptions?

4. Marketing & Channels

  • Acquisition: How will students find you (e.g., local ads, word-of-mouth, social media, platforms like Twinkl)?

  • Onboarding: What is the first step a client takes to book a session with you?

5. Costs & Equipment

  • Overhead Expenses: What tools do you pay for (e.g., video conferencing software, lesson planning apps like Notion, printed materials)?

  • Break-Even Point: How many students or billable hours do you need each month to cover your costs?

6. Monthly Goals & Seasonality

  • Income Target: What is your target monthly revenue?

  • School Year Cycle: How will you account for peak periods (term-time) and slow periods (school holidays) in your cash flow?

#

For your Quarto/GitHub Pages site, I’d use Calendly + Stripe for the quickest route to paid bookings. You can embed Calendly directly in a .qmd page, and it supports collecting payment when someone books, including in euros. The upfront-payment feature requires an eligible Calendly plan.

Calendly Help

+1

The setup can cover both online and in-person lessons, each lasting 60 minutes. You don’t need to build a payment system or store card details yourself.

1. Set up the booking service

  1. Create a Calendly account at calendly.com.

  2. Connect your calendar (Google Calendar or Outlook) so that booked slots aren’t double-booked.

  3. Connect Stripe in Calendly under Integrations & apps → Stripe. You’ll need a Stripe account to receive payments.

    Calendly Help

  4. Create two 60-minute event types: - Online English Lesson — 60 minutes - In-person English Lesson — 60 minutes

    Give each event its own availability and meeting/location instructions.

  5. In each event’s payment settings, enable Require payment to book, select Stripe, set your price in euros, and add your cancellation/refund terms.

    Calendly Help

You can decide whether the in-person lesson happens at your home, at a mutually agreed location, or somewhere else; the event description should make that clear before a student pays.

2. Create booking.qmd

Create a new file called booking.qmd in the same folder as index.qmd and services.qmd.

Paste in this code. Replace YOUR-CALENDLY-USERNAME with your actual Calendly username.

 --- title: "Book a lesson" description: "Book a 60-minute English lesson with Dr Des Ryan." ---  Choose the lesson that suits you and book a time that works for you. Payment is made securely online when you book.  ## Available lessons  - **Online English lesson** — 60 minutes, via video call. - **In-person English lesson** — 60 minutes, at the agreed location.  ## Choose a time  <div class="calendly-inline-widget"      data-url="https://calendly.com/YOUR-CALENDLY-USERNAME"      style="min-width:320px;height:800px;"> </div>  <script src="https://assets.calendly.com/assets/external/widget.js"         async></script>  If the calendar does not appear, [open my booking page directly](https://calendly.com/YOUR-CALENDLY-USERNAME).

This embeds your main Calendly booking page, where visitors can choose between your two event types. Calendly also provides a code generator if you want to embed just one specific event type.

Calendly Help

+1

3. Add Booking to your navigation

In _quarto.yml, add a Booking link to the existing navigation list. For example:

      - href: booking.qmd         text: Book a lesson

Keep the indentation consistent with your other navigation entries.

4. Add a button to your homepage

In index.qmd, add a prominent booking link near the top:

[Book a lesson](booking.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

5. Test before publishing

  1. Run quarto preview and open the booking page.

  2. Check that the calendar loads and displays both lesson types.

  3. Test the booking flow, availability, location details and payment settings.

  4. Publish using your usual GitHub Pages workflow, then test the live website on desktop and mobile.

Important: don’t publish the booking page as ready to accept paid bookings until you’ve connected Stripe, set your actual prices, confirmed the available times and checked the cancellation terms.

One decision to make before you go live

What do you want to charge for a 60-minute lesson? If you already have a price in mind, use it for both event types initially—or set separate prices if in-person lessons involve extra travel. Once you have the price and Calendly username, the code above is ready to personalise.
